newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK dips as market nods on Q1 results.
newsitem.headline: TVK dips as market nods on Q1 results.

text.p: Share prices in Hungarian chemicals company TVK dipped on Monday despite strong first quarter results, traders said.

They said the fall stemmed from the fact that expectations of strong first quarter earnings were already factored into TVK's price which reached a new record high of 3,005 forints last Wednesday, rather than as a reaction to the earnings.

"TVK's earnings were already built into its price," said Laszlo Baranyai of Gog Securities. "Some investors may sell with the aim of profit-taking...but this isn't a substantial fall," he said, adding that buyers appeared at lower levels.
TVK opened at 2,920 forints, below Wednesday's close of 2,945. At 1025 GMT it traded at 2,935 forints.
This morning TVK reported its IAS unconsolidated net income rising to 2.748 billion forints in the January-March period of 1997 from 1.717 billion in the same three months of 1996.
Another trader said an around five percent fall in early trading in prices of oil and gas company MOL shares might have had a negative impact on TVK's prices.
"MOL's fall may be one reason behind TVK's dip," said Robert Forgo of MKB Securities.
